options.label: Vanilla-Shaped
options.tagline: A technology is an invention, and an invention lifts several industries at once.
options.blurb: Keeps vanilla's topology and its shared technologies — `manufacturies` still unlocks six industries' first rung — and extends it only where our ladder has rungs vanilla never had. Smallest tree, cheapest research, most familiar to a returning player. Its cost is paid at roadmap step 2: a shared technology cannot be rewarded to one industry.

techs.name: Atmospheric Engine
techs.reEra: era 2 -> 1: Newcomen 1712, 124 years before era 2 opens

techs.name: Beet Sugar Refining
techs.desc: Marggraf and Achard's beet process frees the sugar trade from the cane colonies, and puts a refinery within reach of any temperate country with a food industry.

techs.name: Calico Printing
techs.desc: Roller printing and the integrated dye works turn cloth finishing from a craft into a chemical trade, and make patterned cloth a mass commodity.

techs.name: Lead Crystal
techs.renamed: It unlocks the LEADED glassworks; the crystal tier is a rung above it, on the regenerative furnace.
techs.reEra: era 2 -> 1: Ravenscroft 1674, 162 years before era 2 opens

techs.name: Fourdrinier Machine
techs.desc: Continuous web papermaking replaces the vatman's mould. Paper stops being sold by the sheet and starts being sold by the mile.

techs.name: Leblanc Process
techs.desc: Soda from salt and sulfuric acid founds the heavy chemical trade — and with it the first works able to make explosives on an industrial scale.

techs.name: Ammoniacal Liquor Recovery
techs.desc: The gasworks and the coke oven were throwing away their ammonia; recovered as sulphate it becomes the first nitrogen fertilizer a country can make rather than import.

techs.name: Compound Expansion
techs.desc: Working the steam twice, through a high-pressure and then a low-pressure cylinder, roughly halves the coal per horsepower-hour — and makes the engine works a supplier to shipping rather than to mills alone.

techs.name: Iron Screw Steamers
techs.desc: The Great Britain: iron hull, screw propeller, no sail worth the name. A yard that can build her is not a yard that built clippers.

techs.name: Steamship Bunkering
techs.desc: A steamer cannot cross an ocean without a coaling station at the other end. Ports rebuild themselves around the bunker, the tug and the tide dock.

techs.name: Steel Hulls
techs.desc: Mild steel plate is stronger than iron for the same weight, so the same hull carries more cargo or more armour, and the yard's berths are laid out for a material that will not be replaced this century.

techs.name: Deep Water Docks
techs.desc: Hydraulic cranes, dredged approaches and enclosed basins let a port handle an iron steamer of a draught no tidal quay could ever take.

techs.name: Filled Explosive Shells
techs.desc: Shells filled and fused on a production line rather than in a laboratory, in quantities a siege can actually spend.

techs.name: Fat Hydrogenation
techs.desc: Normann's nickel catalyst hardens cheap liquid oils into a solid cooking fat, and the food industry stops depending on animal tallow and the dairy herd.

techs.name: Oil Drilling
techs.renamed: It unlocks the oil rig, which is Drake 1859. The pumpjack itself is 1925 and cannot be what gates an era-3 building.

techs.name: Regenerative Furnace
techs.desc: Siemens' heat-recovery tank furnace runs continuously instead of in pots, halving the fuel a glasshouse burns for every ton it melts.

techs.name: Rotary-Cut Veneer
techs.desc: Peeling a log on a rotary lathe and gluing the sheets crosswise gives a panel stronger than the timber it came from, and furniture stops being carpentry and starts being assembly.

techs.name: Steel Toolmaking
techs.desc: Cheap bulk steel reaches the toolmaker. Cutters that once had to be forged from crucible stock are now made from mill steel and hardened in quantity.

techs.name: Steam Threshing
techs.renamed: Vanilla's own comment says it unlocks Steam Threshers. The bare threshing machine is Meikle, 1786, and does not belong in era 3.

techs.name: Wireless Telegraphy
techs.desc: Spark transmitters put a telegraph office on a ship and then across an ocean, and the electrical trade acquires a product that needs no line at all.

techs.name: Reinforced Concrete Quays
techs.desc: Monolithic concrete replaces the timber pile and the masonry block, and a berth can be built where no quarry could ever have supplied one.

techs.name: Diesel Engine
techs.desc: Compression ignition burns a fuel no boiler would take, at an efficiency no steam plant can reach, in a works that can build one to order.

techs.name: Drawn Brass Cartridges
techs.desc: Deep-drawn cases and smokeless powder, loaded by automatic machinery. Ammunition becomes a volume manufacture like any other.

techs.name: Electric Motors
techs.desc: The polyphase induction motor gives every machine its own prime mover. Line shafting, and the mill built around it, begins to disappear.

techs.name: Alternating Current
techs.renamed: It gates electric drive in mills, brine electrolysis and electric saws — polyphase distribution, not a component. A capacitor is the Leyden jar, 1745.

techs.name: High Speed Steel
techs.desc: Taylor and White's tungsten steel cuts red-hot without losing its edge. Machine shop speeds go from five metres a minute to thirty.

techs.name: Kraft Process
techs.desc: Sulfate pulping digests resinous softwoods that sulfite cannot touch, and recovers its own chemicals — the strongest and cheapest pulp yet made.

techs.name: Light Machine Guns
techs.desc: An automatic weapon a section can carry moves sustained fire from the strongpoint into the assault, and the arms industry starts making mechanisms rather than barrels.

techs.name: Long-Draft Spinning
techs.desc: Drafting the roving further in one passage removes whole banks of machinery from the spinning room, and with individual electric drive the mill is rebuilt around the operative rather than the shaft.

techs.name: Marine Steam Turbine
techs.desc: Parsons' turbine at sea: fewer moving parts, no reciprocating mass, and speeds a triple-expansion engine cannot reach.

techs.name: Ostwald Process
techs.desc: Catalytic oxidation of ammonia makes nitric acid without a nitrate mine, and cuts the last colonial tether on the explosives trade.

techs.name: Recoil Carriages
techs.desc: The French 75's hydro-pneumatic recoil keeps the barrel on target between rounds, and multiplies a battery's rate of fire.

techs.name: Semi-Chemical Pulping
techs.desc: A mild sulfite cook followed by mechanical defibring opens hardwoods the chemical mills could not use, and the corrugated box gets a cheap domestic furnish.

techs.name: Mass Shell Filling
techs.desc: The filling factory is a distinct industry from the case plant: acres of separated sheds, women's labour at scale, and an output measured in millions of rounds a week.

techs.name: Superheating
techs.desc: Passing the steam back through the firebox before it reaches the cylinders cuts coal and water by about a quarter per ton-mile, and is why the steam locomotive survived the electric one by forty years.

techs.name: Synthetic Indigo
techs.desc: Seventeen years and a fortune later, BASF sells indigo made from coal tar — and the Bengal indigo districts have nothing left to sell.

techs.name: Autofrettage
techs.desc: Pre-stressing a barrel from within replaces built-up hoop construction — a lighter gun of the same power, made in fewer operations.

techs.name: Automatic Anti-Aircraft Guns
techs.desc: A fast-traversing automatic gun on a welded mounting, laid by a mechanical director, is the first artillery designed for a target that moves faster than the shell's flight time.

techs.name: Automatic Cartridge Lines
techs.desc: Case, primer, powder and bullet joined by machines that need a setter rather than an operator.

techs.name: Cemented Carbide
techs.desc: Tungsten carbide sintered in cobalt cuts four to seven times faster than high speed steel, and wears out far more slowly.

techs.name: Continuous Nitration
techs.desc: Nitration in a flowing stream rather than a batch pot — safer, steadier, and limited only by how fast acid can be pumped.

techs.name: Continuous Wide Strip Mill
techs.desc: Armco's continuous mill rolls a coil of wide sheet in one pass. It is the largest single step interwar steel takes, and vanilla has no tier for it at all.

techs.name: Cyclonite Process
techs.desc: Nitrating hexamine gives an explosive half again as powerful as TNT, and continuous plant makes it in quantities that change what a bomb and a torpedo can do.

techs.name: Mechanised Bakeries
techs.renamed: It unlocks the whole automated bakery, of which the dough roller is one machine — and in our ladder it is a tier building.

techs.name: Glass Fibre
techs.desc: Glass drawn continuously into filaments finer than wool is no longer a glazing material at all — it insulates, reinforces and filters, and the glassworks acquires a market that has nothing to do with windows.

techs.name: High Speed Diesel
techs.desc: Welded frames and light alloys take the diesel from a stationary engine to something a lorry, a locomotive or a submarine can carry.

techs.name: High Speed Papermaking
techs.desc: Suction presses, steam drying and precision drives take the Fourdrinier past a quarter mile of paper a minute.

techs.name: Mechanised Cargo Handling
techs.desc: Travelling gantries, conveyors and motor trucks on the quay. A motor ship's turnaround is measured in days rather than weeks.

techs.name: Nitrocellulose Lacquers
techs.desc: Sprayed lacquer dries in minutes where varnish took days. Furniture finishing stops being the bottleneck of the whole trade.

techs.name: Oil-Fired Boilers
techs.desc: Oil firing halves the stokehold crew and doubles the range. The yard's customers stop specifying coal bunkers.

techs.name: Polyamide Synthesis
techs.desc: Carothers' nylon is the first fibre owing nothing to a plant or an animal — and the first that competes with silk on its own terms.

techs.name: Pulverized Coal Firing
techs.desc: Coal ground to flour and blown into the furnace burns like a gas. Station units jump from single megawatts to tens of them.

techs.name: Ribbon Machine
techs.desc: Corning's ribbon machine blows bulbs from a moving ribbon of glass at a rate no gathering machine can approach.

techs.name: Sound Film
techs.desc: Synchronised sound, and then colour. The academy's product stops being a picture and becomes a performance.

techs.name: Stamped Receivers
techs.desc: Pressed and welded sheet metal in place of milled forgings. A weapon a bicycle works can make, in the numbers a war needs.

techs.name: Steam Reforming
techs.desc: Hydrogen from methane instead of coke. The ammonia plant sheds its gasworks and its coal yard together.

techs.name: Hydraulic Tracer Control
techs.desc: A stylus follows a master form and hydraulics repeat it on the cutter, so a complex profile no longer needs a skilled machinist — only a first article to copy.

techs.name: Transfer Machining
techs.desc: Workpieces are indexed automatically from station to station. The assembly line finally reaches the machine shop feeding it.

techs.name: Vacuum Tube Electronics
techs.desc: Amplification makes the valve a component rather than a curiosity, and turns the telephone works into an electronics industry.

options.label: Industry Ladders
options.tagline: A technology is a step in one industry's history.
options.blurb: One dedicated technology per tier: 22 near-independent verticals, with cross-links only where a recipe literally cannot exist without another industry's product. Maximum per-industry targeting, which is what the industry-driven research events need; reads like an industry's own story. Weakest at making a technological lead in one sector lift the others.

options.label: Platform & Application
options.tagline: A technology is either a general-purpose capability or its application to one industry.
options.blurb: Option 2's ladders plus a backbone of nine platform technologies, each tier technology also requiring the platform of its generation. The strongest realisation of "a technological edge should really matter": neglect steel, precision or electricity and every industry stalls at once. Biggest and densest tree, and the one that leans hardest on the ahead-of-time penalty.

techs.renamed: It unlocks the oil rig, which is Drake 1859. The pumpjack itself is 1925 and cannot be what gates an era-3 building.

techs.name: Regenerative Furnace
techs.desc: Siemens' heat-recovery tank furnace runs continuously instead of in pots, halving the fuel a glasshouse burns for every ton it melts.

techs.name: Rotary-Cut Veneer
techs.desc: Peeling a log on a rotary lathe and gluing the sheets crosswise gives a panel stronger than the timber it came from, and furniture stops being carpentry and starts being assembly.

techs.name: Steel Toolmaking
techs.desc: Cheap bulk steel reaches the toolmaker. Cutters that once had to be forged from crucible stock are now made from mill steel and hardened in quantity.

techs.name: Sulfite Pulping
techs.desc: Tilghman's acid digestion turns standing timber into paper, and rag supply stops being the ceiling on how much a country can print.

techs.name: Steam Threshing
techs.renamed: Vanilla's own comment says it unlocks Steam Threshers. The bare threshing machine is Meikle, 1786, and does not belong in era 3.

techs.name: Wireless Telegraphy
techs.desc: Spark transmitters put a telegraph office on a ship and then across an ocean, and the electrical trade acquires a product that needs no line at all.

techs.name: Alloy Steels
techs.desc: Manganese, nickel, chromium, tungsten. Steel stops being one material and becomes a catalogue of them.

techs.name: Reinforced Concrete Quays
techs.desc: Monolithic concrete replaces the timber pile and the masonry block, and a berth can be built where no quarry could ever have supplied one.

techs.name: Diesel Engine
techs.desc: Compression ignition burns a fuel no boiler would take, at an efficiency no steam plant can reach, in a works that can build one to order.

techs.name: Drawn Brass Cartridges
techs.desc: Deep-drawn cases and smokeless powder, loaded by automatic machinery. Ammunition becomes a volume manufacture like any other.

techs.name: Electric Drive
techs.desc: Power delivered as wire rather than as shafting. Every industry gets to rebuild its floor plan around its process.

techs.name: Electric Drive Looms
techs.desc: Individual motor drive per loom ends the overhead shaft, and lets a weaving shed be laid out for the cloth instead of for the belting.

techs.name: Electric Motors
techs.desc: The polyphase induction motor gives every machine its own prime mover. Line shafting, and the mill built around it, begins to disappear.

techs.name: Alternating Current
techs.renamed: It gates electric drive in mills, brine electrolysis and electric saws — polyphase distribution, not a component. A capacitor is the Leyden jar, 1745.

techs.name: High Speed Steel
techs.desc: Taylor and White's tungsten steel cuts red-hot without losing its edge. Machine shop speeds go from five metres a minute to thirty.

techs.name: Industrial Catalysis
techs.desc: A bed of platinum, and a reaction that would not otherwise run. The chemical works stops distilling nature and starts building molecules.

techs.name: Kraft Process
techs.desc: Sulfate pulping digests resinous softwoods that sulfite cannot touch, and recovers its own chemicals — the strongest and cheapest pulp yet made.

techs.name: Light Machine Guns
techs.desc: An automatic weapon a section can carry moves sustained fire from the strongpoint into the assault, and the arms industry starts making mechanisms rather than barrels.

techs.name: Long-Draft Spinning
techs.desc: Drafting the roving further in one passage removes whole banks of machinery from the spinning room, and with individual electric drive the mill is rebuilt around the operative rather than the shaft.

techs.name: Marine Steam Turbine
techs.desc: Parsons' turbine at sea: fewer moving parts, no reciprocating mass, and speeds a triple-expansion engine cannot reach.

techs.name: Ostwald Process
techs.desc: Catalytic oxidation of ammonia makes nitric acid without a nitrate mine, and cuts the last colonial tether on the explosives trade.

techs.name: Recoil Carriages
techs.desc: The French 75's hydro-pneumatic recoil keeps the barrel on target between rounds, and multiplies a battery's rate of fire.

techs.name: Scientific Management
techs.desc: Time study, routing and the planning department. The bottleneck moves from what a machine can do to how the work reaches it.

techs.name: Semi-Chemical Pulping
techs.desc: A mild sulfite cook followed by mechanical defibring opens hardwoods the chemical mills could not use, and the corrugated box gets a cheap domestic furnish.

techs.name: Mass Shell Filling
techs.desc: The filling factory is a distinct industry from the case plant: acres of separated sheds, women's labour at scale, and an output measured in millions of rounds a week.

techs.name: Superheating
techs.desc: Passing the steam back through the firebox before it reaches the cylinders cuts coal and water by about a quarter per ton-mile, and is why the steam locomotive survived the electric one by forty years.

techs.name: Synthetic Indigo
techs.desc: Seventeen years and a fortune later, BASF sells indigo made from coal tar — and the Bengal indigo districts have nothing left to sell.

techs.name: Autofrettage
techs.desc: Pre-stressing a barrel from within replaces built-up hoop construction — a lighter gun of the same power, made in fewer operations.

techs.name: Automatic Anti-Aircraft Guns
techs.desc: A fast-traversing automatic gun on a welded mounting, laid by a mechanical director, is the first artillery designed for a target that moves faster than the shell's flight time.

techs.name: Automatic Cartridge Lines
techs.desc: Case, primer, powder and bullet joined by machines that need a setter rather than an operator.

techs.name: Cemented Carbide
techs.desc: Tungsten carbide sintered in cobalt cuts four to seven times faster than high speed steel, and wears out far more slowly.

techs.name: Continuous Nitration
techs.desc: Nitration in a flowing stream rather than a batch pot — safer, steadier, and limited only by how fast acid can be pumped.

techs.name: Continuous Wide Strip Mill
techs.desc: Armco's continuous mill rolls a coil of wide sheet in one pass. It is the largest single step interwar steel takes, and vanilla has no tier for it at all.

techs.name: Cyclonite Process
techs.desc: Nitrating hexamine gives an explosive half again as powerful as TNT, and continuous plant makes it in quantities that change what a bomb and a torpedo can do.

techs.name: Mechanised Bakeries
techs.renamed: It unlocks the whole automated bakery, of which the dough roller is one machine — and in our ladder it is a tier building.

techs.name: Glass Fibre
techs.desc: Glass drawn continuously into filaments finer than wool is no longer a glazing material at all — it insulates, reinforces and filters, and the glassworks acquires a market that has nothing to do with windows.

techs.name: High Speed Diesel
techs.desc: Welded frames and light alloys take the diesel from a stationary engine to something a lorry, a locomotive or a submarine can carry.

techs.name: High Speed Papermaking
techs.desc: Suction presses, steam drying and precision drives take the Fourdrinier past a quarter mile of paper a minute.

techs.name: Light Alloys
techs.desc: Duralumin and its relatives: strength without weight, and a machining problem every industry has to learn.

techs.name: Mechanised Cargo Handling
techs.desc: Travelling gantries, conveyors and motor trucks on the quay. A motor ship's turnaround is measured in days rather than weeks.

techs.name: Nitrocellulose Lacquers
techs.desc: Sprayed lacquer dries in minutes where varnish took days. Furniture finishing stops being the bottleneck of the whole trade.

techs.name: Oil-Fired Boilers
techs.desc: Oil firing halves the stokehold crew and doubles the range. The yard's customers stop specifying coal bunkers.

techs.name: Polyamide Synthesis
techs.desc: Carothers' nylon is the first fibre owing nothing to a plant or an animal — and the first that competes with silk on its own terms.

techs.name: Process Control
techs.desc: Instruments that hold a process on its setpoint without a hand on the valve — continuous production's missing precondition.

techs.name: Pulverized Coal Firing
techs.desc: Coal ground to flour and blown into the furnace burns like a gas. Station units jump from single megawatts to tens of them.

techs.name: Ribbon Machine
techs.desc: Corning's ribbon machine blows bulbs from a moving ribbon of glass at a rate no gathering machine can approach.

techs.name: Sound Film
techs.desc: Synchronised sound, and then colour. The academy's product stops being a picture and becomes a performance.

techs.name: Stamped Receivers
techs.desc: Pressed and welded sheet metal in place of milled forgings. A weapon a bicycle works can make, in the numbers a war needs.

techs.name: Steam Reforming
techs.desc: Hydrogen from methane instead of coke. The ammonia plant sheds its gasworks and its coal yard together.

techs.name: Hydraulic Tracer Control
techs.desc: A stylus follows a master form and hydraulics repeat it on the cutter, so a complex profile no longer needs a skilled machinist — only a first article to copy.

techs.name: Transfer Machining
techs.desc: Workpieces are indexed automatically from station to station. The assembly line finally reaches the machine shop feeding it.

techs.name: Vacuum Tube Electronics
techs.desc: Amplification makes the valve a component rather than a curiosity, and turns the telephone works into an electronics industry.
